We can find the roots of a quadratic equation using the quadratic formula:

$$
x=\frac{-b\pm \sqrt{{b}^{2}-4ac}}{2a}
$$

In this case, the coefficients are $a=1,\,b=-12,$ and $c=40.$ Substituting these values into the quadratic formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{12\pm \sqrt{(-12)^{2}-4(1)(40)}}{2(1)} \\  & =\frac{12\pm \sqrt{144-160}}{2} \\  & =\frac{12\pm \sqrt{-16}}{2} \\  & =\frac{12\pm 4\,\text{i}}{2} \\  & =6\pm 2\,\text{i}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation has two solutions, $x=6+2\text{i}$ and $x=6-2\text{i}.$

We wish to add the following fractions:

$$
t+r=\frac{7v}{2(3+2v)}+\frac{3-5v}{3+2v}
$$

In order to add the two fractions, we need them to have a common denominator. Here, we can put both fractions over a common denominator of $2(3+2v)$ if we multiply the top and bottom of the second fraction by $2:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{7v}{2(3+2v)}+\frac{3-5v}{3+2v} & = \\ \frac{7v}{2(3+2v)}+\frac{2}{2}\cdot \frac{3-5v}{3+2v} & = \\ \frac{7v}{2(3+2v)}+\frac{2(3-5v)}{2(3+2v)} & = \\ \frac{7v+2(3-5v)}{2(3+2v)} & = \\ \frac{7v+6-10v}{2(3+2v)} & = \\ \frac{6-3v}{2(3+2v)} & = \\ \frac{3(2-v)}{2(3+2v)}\end{aligned}
$$

The equation of the vertical asymptote of the function $y=\operatorname{log}⁡x$ is $x=0.$

To find the equation of the vertical asymptote of $f(x),$ we set the argument of the logarithmic term equal to zero, and solve for $x.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}2-x & =0 \\ -x & =-2 \\ x & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the vertical asymptote is $x=2.$
